sentences.en: Hello and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big changes and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《你的二十多岁心理学》，在这里我们探讨二十多岁时的一些重大变化与转型，以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Big topic this week, big topic for our 20s as well.
sentences.zh: 本周是大主题，这也是我们二十多岁时的一大主题。

sentences.en: We're talking about interpersonal conflict of all sorts on this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在本期节目中要讨论各种各样的人际冲突。

sentences.en: We're talking about fighting.
sentences.zh: 我们在讨论争吵。

sentences.en: We're talking about the drama of arguments, of fights with family, of friends.
sentences.zh: 我们在讨论争执的戏剧性，以及与家人、朋友的争吵。

sentences.en: It's pretty normal to have conflict with people as we're figuring ourselves out, but also in general, not just in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 在我们探索自我的过程中，与他人产生冲突其实是很正常的，而且不仅仅是在二十多岁，生活中本就如此。

sentences.en: We fight and we start conflict when we're misunderstood, when we feel underappreciated, slighted, betrayed, and for no reason at all, really.
sentences.zh: 当我们被误解、感到不被赏识、被轻视、被背叛，甚至其实毫无理由时，我们就会争吵并挑起冲突。

sentences.en: I think fights between our friends, our partners, maybe our colleagues, definitely our families.
sentences.zh: 我认为朋友、伴侣、同事之间，当然还有家人之间的争吵，

sentences.en: It's a real normal part of daily life.
sentences.zh: 是日常生活非常正常的一部分。

sentences.en: Maybe not daily life, but life in general.
sentences.zh: 也许不一定是日常生活，但绝对是人生常态。

sentences.en: So today I really want to discuss the psychology behind why we have conflict with people, maybe some more than others, why we can't let things go,
sentences.zh: 所以今天我真的很想讨论为什么我们会与人产生冲突的背后心理，为什么有些人之间的冲突会比其他人更多，为什么我们总是放不下事情，

sentences.en: why we rehearse arguments in our head, and how to release anger towards another person.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会在脑海里排练争论的场景，以及如何释放对另一个人的愤怒。

sentences.en: Psychology has so much to say about interpersonal conflict.
sentences.zh: 心理学对人际冲突有很多见解。

sentences.en: It's a massive part of social psychology.
sentences.zh: 这是社会心理学中极其重要的一部分。

sentences.en: So let's dive right in.
sentences.zh: 那我们现在就开始吧。

sentences.en: I don't think we need a definition of conflict, unless you are the most peaceful person in the world.
sentences.zh: 我想我们不需要对冲突下一个定义，除非你是世界上最爱好和平的人。

sentences.en: I'm sure we've all had a fight with someone or a disagreement of some kind that went a little bit too far.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，我们都曾与某人发生过争吵或某种有点过头的意见不合。

sentences.en: It's a pretty nasty feeling.
sentences.zh: 那真是一种很不舒服的感觉。

sentences.en: It's an anxious feeling to be fighting with someone close to us, especially when we don't really know how it's going to work out or if things can be fixed.
sentences.zh: 与我们亲近的人争吵会带来焦虑感，尤其是当我们并不真正知道事情会如何收场，或者问题是否能解决时。

sentences.en: I don't think that fighting with others into personal conflict is avoidable, but we can make it easier on ourselves and others and have happy outcomes
sentences.zh: 我认为与他人发生人际冲突是无法避免的，但我们可以让自己和他人好过一些，收获快乐的结果，

sentences.en: rather than disastrous ones, I guess.
sentences.zh: 而不是灾难性的结果，我想是的。

sentences.en: So there are many reasons that conflict in our interpersonal relationships may arise, maybe even more common with people we love or who we're close to
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的人际关系中之所以会出现冲突，原因有很多，在面对我们爱的人或亲近的人时，这种冲突可能甚至更常见，

sentences.en: because we feel comfortable enough to express our anger and our insecurities.
sentences.zh: 因为我们感到足够舒适，可以表达我们的愤怒和不安全感。

sentences.en: We're also more likely to feel misunderstood by the people we believe should understand us.
sentences.zh: 我们也更容易从那些我们认为应该理解我们的人身上感到被误解。

sentences.en: So that perception of feeling misunderstood, perhaps it's not the reality that they don't understand you.
sentences.zh: 所以这种感到被误解的看法，也许现实并非他们不理解你。

sentences.en: They probably understand you more than most people, but that perception that they should know, they should know how you'd be feeling.
sentences.zh: 他们可能比大多数人更理解你，但那种“他们应该懂”的看法觉得他们应该知道你的感受。

sentences.en: They should know how you'd react to their words, to their actions.
sentences.zh: 他们应该知道你对他们的话、他们的行为会有什么反应。

sentences.en: So yeah, I think when we have people close to us, it's probably more common that we have that conflict with them.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为当我们身边有亲近的人时，与他们发生这种冲突可能会更常见。

sentences.en: And I think although there's a lot of dialogue around how fighting is healthy for your relationships, which it is, and we'll discuss why,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，尽管有很多关于争吵对人际关系有益的讨论（确实如此，我们稍后会讨论原因），

sentences.en: it doesn't always lead to the best outcomes in the moment or in the long run.
sentences.zh: 它并不总能在当下或长远带来最好的结果。

sentences.en: If you're screaming at someone, you're probably not listening to their perspective.
sentences.zh: 如果你在大声冲别人吼叫，你大概就没在听他们的观点。

sentences.en: If you're really mad, it's very hard to see where they might be coming from.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的很生气，就很难站在他们的角度去思考。

sentences.en: And it's hard to express where you're coming from as well.
sentences.zh: 而且也很难表达你自己的立场。

sentences.en: Arguing and fighting can actually lead to worse outcomes because we don't sit back and think about both sides of the narrative.
sentences.zh: 争辩和争吵实际上可能会导致更糟糕的结果，因为我们不会坐下来思考叙事的双方。

sentences.en: Take this study, for example.
sentences.zh: 以这项研究为例。

sentences.en: So a study of nurses found that when they argued about patient care on the treatment floor, they were less likely to arrive at a good decision and lost focus on the task at hand
sentences.zh: 一项针对护士的研究发现，当他们在病房里就患者护理问题发生争执时，他们更难做出正确的决定，并且会转移对当前任务的注意力，

sentences.en: in favor of the interpersonal conflict.
sentences.zh: 转而把焦点放在人际冲突上。

sentences.en: That's a pretty real world example.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常现实的例子。

sentences.en: You know, they're not able to actually provide care as well if fighting and conflict is getting in the way.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果争吵和冲突从中作梗，他们就无法真正提供好护理。

sentences.en: So where does this kind of nastiness, not so much nastiness, I don't want to use the word conflict again,
sentences.zh: 那么，这种不快——倒也不是说不快，我不想再用“冲突”这个词——

sentences.en: these disruptions to the harmony of our relationships, yeah, where does fighting come from?
sentences.zh: 这种对我们关系和谐的破坏，是的，争吵究竟是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: Why does it occur?
sentences.zh: 为什么会发生这种事？

sentences.en: Anger at someone can come from quite a few places, obviously.
sentences.zh: 对某人的愤怒显然可以源于很多地方。

sentences.en: And there's a few main reasons that psychologists have kind of identified as the leading causes of arguments amongst people.
sentences.zh: 心理学家已经确定了导致人吉之间争吵的几个主要原因。

sentences.en: So firstly, and we've already mentioned this, but you feel misunderstood.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们之前已经提到过了，你觉得自己被误解了。

sentences.en: Misunderstandings are common and they're often innocuous, yet they can create conflict, as I'm sure we're all aware.
sentences.zh: 误解是很常见的，而且通常是无恶意的，但正如我们所知，它们会引发冲突。

sentences.en: Perhaps someone has misheard something you've said and now they're angry with you.
sentences.zh: 也许有人听错了你的话，现在生你的气了。

sentences.en: Perhaps they heard your words correctly, but comprehended them in a manner that did not align with your intent.
sentences.zh: 也许他们听清了你的话，但理解的方式与你的本意并不相符。

sentences.en: Or perhaps they interpreted your silence in a way that was consistent or inconsistent with the message you wanted to send.
sentences.zh: 或者也许他们对你沉默的解读，与你想传达的信息一致或不一致。

sentences.en: Importantly, people aren't mind readers.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，人们不会读心术。

sentences.en: My therapist says this to me all the time.
sentences.zh: 我的治疗师总是对我说这句话。

sentences.en: Perception and intention are completely different and our intentions aren't always clear and it's an effort to always have to deliberately signpost exactly what you mean
sentences.zh: 感知和意图完全是两码事，我们的意图并不总是清晰的，刻意去准确标明你的真实意思需要付出努力，

sentences.en: and it's difficult for people to pick up on what we're really saying if we're not being clear.
sentences.zh: 如果我们表达得不够清楚，别人很难领会我们真正想说的话。

sentences.en: So similar to this feeling misunderstood in a more general sense, maybe the way someone has treated you or something they've said really contradicts how you see yourself
sentences.zh: 因此，类似于这种更普遍意义上的被误解，也许别人的对待方式或说过的话，与你对自己的看法以及你认为重要的身份认同感相矛盾。

sentences.en: and aspects of your identity that you think are important.
sentences.zh: 因此，你觉得自己受到了他们对你的那种看法的攻击。

sentences.en: So you feel attacked by what you perceive their kind of idea of you as being.
sentences.zh: 你觉得他们对你的看法被误解了。

sentences.en: You feel misunderstood by how you believe they see you.
sentences.zh: 不管来源如何，如果不迅速处理，误解确实会破坏人际关系。

sentences.en: Regardless of their source, misunderstandings can really damage relationships if they're not handled swiftly.
sentences.zh: 首先，你应该扪心自问，自己是否真的被误解了，或者对方对情况的解读是否有其道理。

sentences.en: First, you should really ask yourself if you're actually being misunderstood or if the other person's read of the situation is maybe warranted.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们常常倾向于优待自己的观点并假定其客观性，而实际上我们所说的话确实可以有多种解读方式。

sentences.en: I think often we privilege our viewpoints and presume objectivity when in fact what we said can indeed be interpreted in so many ways.

sentences.en: Like I said people can't read your mind so if you're not clear about your reaction to their actions or words resentment can start to build.
